A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CAML and contain readable methods, experiments, figures, tables, and appendices. Content can be matched reliably despite substantial reorganization and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulated driving evaluations, real-world CoPeD segmentation results, a fusion-order ablation, and measured training costs.

after.justification: v2 retains original driving and segmentation evaluations and adds teacher/RGB-only comparisons and communication/inference measurements.

M1.justification: The architecture, feature aggregation, teacher–student procedure, and pre-fusion variant remain. However, Appendix A.5 changes the specified distillation temperature from 3.0 to 4.0 and loss weight alpha from 0.5 to 0.9, modifying soft targets and the balance of the student objective.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same overtaking, left-turn, and red-light-violation driving scenarios and CoPeD's indoor NYUARPL and outdoor HOUSEA segmentation scenarios. Single-agent deployment and noisy ground-robot inputs were already evaluated in v1. Modality dropout and communication failures remain future work.

E2.justification: v2 adds the fully equipped teacher and RGB-only multi-agent BC comparators in Table 2. It removes AML from the single-agent generalization comparison, matching v1 Figure 5 to v2 Figure 4. The principal external comparator families remain AML, COOPERNAUT, STGN, and FCN.

E3.justification: v2 introduces collaborative COOPERNAUT evaluation and uses cooperative COOPERNAUT/STGN settings in the main driving comparison; v1 already evaluated cooperative STGN separately. It adds shared-package-size and per-batch latency evaluations and teacher/RGB-only controls. Appendix A.5 also revises distillation settings. The 12/12 trial split and training budget remain unchanged; these reported revisions do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New driving ablations compare CAML with its full-modality teacher and a collaborative RGB-only model without distillation, examining the cost of modality removal and benefit of auxiliary-modality learning. v2 also adds communication/inference efficiency analysis. The single-agent generalization test, segmentation examples, and pre-fusion ablation are retained.

E5.justification: v1 supplies driving point estimates without run counts or uncertainty reporting. v2 Section 4.1 first reports four repeated runs and means with standard deviations, displayed in the driving plots and Table 2. This substantially changes uncertainty reporting without establishing an increase over v1's unspecified run count.

E6.justification: Driving results change: for example, CAML's left-turn ADR is 66.32% in v1 Figure 3 and 67.3±1.0% in v2 Figure 3. Revised distillation settings prevent interpreting this as a same-setting gain. New results include the teacher/RGB-only comparisons and CAML's 1.0 KB package size and 3.7 ms latency. Segmentation, pre-fusion, and training-complexity results are retained apart from rounding.

T1.justification: v2 removes v1 Section 4's Gaussian prior/likelihood assumptions, posterior-variance formulas, and uncertainty-reduction argument. Appendix A.1 adds a chain-rule derivation supporting the retained mutual-information inequality and discusses redundant observations. The data-coverage definitions and centralized/decentralized complexity expressions remain.

C1.justification: The standalone theoretical-analysis contribution disappears from the abstract and contribution list. The conclusion replaces theoretical uncertainty-reduction claims with an intuitive data-coverage/information-gain analysis, substantially narrowing the claimed analytical contribution. The CAML framework and headline empirical claims remain, with numerical rounding.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly characterizes its analysis as intuition rather than a formal performance proof. Appendix A.6 replaces explicit misalignment/noisy-fusion and coordination-delay caveats with fixed modality assignments during student training, reliable training communication, and proposed future modality dropout. New ablation discussion explains the teacher–student performance tradeoff and the benefit over RGB-only collaborative training.

D1.justification: v2 adds expert-agent data-collection details, randomized trial configurations, an approximately 400 GB dataset size, a behavior-cloning subsection, and explicit RGB/LiDAR embedding concatenation. It revises the reported distillation hyperparameters. Hardware, optimizer, batch size, epochs, and measured training costs remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Tian et al.'s Contrastive Representation Distillation citation and removes the CARLA and Murphy Gaussian-analysis references. The related-work coverage and positioning around combining multi-agent collaboration with auxiliary-modality learning otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten. Analysis moves from the main text to Appendix A.1, system complexity moves into Section 3, and segmentation examples and pre-fusion discussion move into the main experiments. The appendices are reorganized, and the generic impact statement is removed.

P2.justification: The main document changes from two-column to predominantly single-column layout. Driving plots are reorganized with revised comparator groupings and uncertainty displays, two experimental tables are added, and the segmentation illustration moves from appendix Figure 8 to main-text Figure 5. Figure captions and table placement also change substantially.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical support: cooperative comparisons, the teacher/RGB-only controls in Table 2, and repeated-run uncertainty address v1's limited isolation of distillation benefits and unquantified variability. Table 1 also supplies deployment-efficiency evidence, while the narrower analytical claims better reflect their support. Some earlier failure caveats are lost, and the multi-agent STGN discussion incorrectly references the single-agent Figure 4, but these drawbacks are outweighed by the improved experimental evidence.
